This is a real, diff-grounded UX/error-messaging issue rather than a functional defect — the mechanism the finding describes is accurate (misleading error message causing user confusion), but behavior is not broken: duplicate adds are correctly blocked. It is a specific, substantive review concern about error semantics in new code, not a defect.

judged_text: When every submitted guest is filtered out because they are already an attendee or blacklisted, the handler throws BAD_REQUEST with message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', which is false in both cases. A user adding an already-invited colleague (the dialog only checks uniqueness within the current input, not against existing attendees) is told their emails are invalid instead of 'already invited', prompting confused retries with the same result.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that are already in `booking.attendees` or in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. If all submitted guests are filtered out, it throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`. That message is indeed misleading in those cases (already-invited or blacklisted are not “invalid/duplicate” per the UI text). The client dialog only validates email format + uniqueness within the submitted array (`z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)`) and does not check against existing attendees/blacklist, so users can hit this path and receive the incorrect error text as the finding describes.
